title: Canada GDP by industry, May 2026
question: What will Statistics Canada first report as the month-over-month percent change in seasonally adjusted real gross domestic product by industry, all industries, at basic prices, for May 2026?
resolutionSource: Statistics Canada The Daily release and Table 36-10-0434-01
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Statistics Canada publication on July 31, 2026 for May 2026 seasonally adjusted real GDP by industry, all industries, month-to-month percent change, rounded to one decimal percentage point. If the July 31, 2026 Daily text and Table 36-10-0434-01 disagree at first publication, use the table value for all industries month-to-month percent change. Ignore later revisions.

reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference-class step: the recent official-source reference class for this exact monthly all-industries GDP-by-industry series is low positive growth. The November-April mean of 0.1, 0.1, 0.0, 0.2, -0.1, and 0.5 is about 0.13 percent, while the median is 0.1 percent.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanisms: the level signal improved after April's broad 0.5 percent rebound, but that rebound leaned on reversals in oil and gas, manufacturing, transportation, and construction. May's advance estimate explicitly says growth slowed to 0.1, so momentum is positive but weak. One-off April catch-up raises payback risk. Trade and tariff uncertainty remain a drag on wholesale and goods activity, while finance, real estate, and public-facing services support a modest positive print.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is the recent first-print/table all-industries monthly reference class from November 2025 through April 2026, centered near 0.1 percent. I update toward Statistics Canada's May advance estimate of 0.1 with small offsets: +0.05 for finance and real estate support, -0.05 for wholesale/agriculture weakness and April payback, leaving a 0.1 rounded point. The 80% interval uses recent realized first-print dispersion and advance-estimate uncertainty, widened for one-decimal rounding and sector payback risk, giving -0.2 to 0.4.

Counter-consideration: the downside case is that April's rebound was a one-month catch-up and May wholesale/agriculture weakness plus softer goods output push the official print to -0.2 or below. The upside case is that finance, real estate, energy, and services strength were understated in the advance estimate and the first print reaches 0.4 or higher.

Point calculation: 0.13 recent average rounded toward the 0.1 May advance estimate = 0.1. Interval calculation: 0.1 minus 0.3 percentage point = -0.2, and 0.1 plus 0.3 percentage point = 0.4, an 80% rounded first-print interval that covers typical recent monthly variation plus advance-estimate miss risk.
